# MCP Tools & Prompts Reference (`informal mcp`)

Complete JSON-RPC Model Context Protocol reference generated directly from `crates/informal-mcp/src/{tools,prompts}.rs`.

- **Core session tools:** 37
- **Desktop window tools (`gui_*`):** 12
- **Server-hosted MCP prompts:** 4

## Error Contract (`informal.error/1`)

Every tool error returns structured JSON (`isError: true`) with actionable Poka-Yoke recovery fields:

```json
{
  "schema": "informal.error/1",
  "code": "not_found",
  "message": "no property named a_mx",
  "hint": "Did you mean `a_max`? Run `property_list` to inspect active properties.",
  "suggested_tool": "property_list",
  "candidates": ["a_max"]
}
```

## MCP Prompts (`prompts/list`, `prompts/get`)

Server-hosted playbooks dynamically hydrated with the active session's top module, port boundary, clocks/reset, and failing/undetermined properties:

| Prompt | Arguments | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `triage_cex` | `property` | Expert root-cause workflow: fuse causal slice + driver snippets via `cex_diagnose`, classify RTL bug vs missing input assumption vs broken SVA, validate any fix with `proposal_validate`, and optionally launch a visual walkthrough via `gui_present_cex`. |
| `close_undetermined` | `property` | Structured convergence ladder for `undetermined` properties: inspect complexity/telemetry via `convergence_diagnose`, mine inductive helper invariants with `proposal_validate(kind="assert")`, or apply sound cutpoint/blackbox/case-split abstractions. |
| `spec_to_sva` | `requirement` (req), `module` | Spec-driven SVA engineering hydrated with the DUT's exact input/output port boundary: write reset-guarded safety assertions paired with non-vacuity witness covers and verify them via `proposal_validate` before proposing. |
| `audit_signoff` | `spec_file` | Run a complete signoff gate across the live session: `spec_audit` against `fvp.spec.json` (if present), `formal_lint`, assumption over-constraint/vacuity audit, `under_ai` provenance review, cover reachability, and `check_cov` COI/UNR coverage. |

## Core Session Tools

### `session_open`

**Open a design** — Start the session over from a JasperGold or VC Formal Tcl script (`script`), or from SystemVerilog files with a top module, clock and reset (`files`). A script runs as written, including any prove in it. Returns the session summary; a script that stops with an error gives ok=false and the error, with the session as far as it got.

- **Availability:** All modes (`read-only`, `propose`, `auto`)
- **Mutates session:** no
- **Reply schema:** `informal.open/1`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clock` | string | no | Clock signal (with files) |
| `files` | array\<string\> | no | SystemVerilog files, instead of a script |
| `flavor` | enum (`jg` \| `vcf`) | no | Command set of the script; detected when left out |
| `reset` | string | no | Condition that holds during reset, e.g. !rst_n (with files) |
| `script` | string | no | Tcl script path |
| `top` | string | no | Top module (with files) |

### `script_check`

**Check a script without running it** — Report, per line, every command or option of a Tcl script that the tool would reject, ignore or does not know. Nothing is elaborated or proved and the open session is not touched.

- **Availability:** All modes (`read-only`, `propose`, `auto`)
- **Mutates session:** no
- **Reply schema:** `informal.check/1`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `flavor` | enum (`jg` \| `vcf`) | no |  |
| `script` | string | yes | Tcl script path |

### `design_info`

**Design information** — What the design holds, counted on its netlist (instances, inputs, flops, latches, memories, clocks and resets found), what the script declared (clocks, reset, black boxes, the current task's cut points and properties), and the size of the current task's model after lowering (Btor2 nodes, states, inputs, constraints, targets, and the bit-blasted AIG). Builds the model, so it takes as long as one lowering.

- **Availability:** All modes (`read-only`, `propose`, `auto`)
- **Mutates session:** no
- **Reply schema:** `informal.design_info/1`

### `trace_get`

**Counterexample or cover trace as data** — The trace of a property whose status is cex or covered: one value per signal and frame (a frame is a clock cycle; frame 0 is the reset cycle). Words are in hex, single bits 0 or 1. hit_at lists the frames in which the assertion fails or the cover is hit. Without `signals`, the signals the property names come first, then the rest of its cone.

- **Availability:** All modes (`read-only`, `propose`, `auto`)
- **Mutates session:** no
- **Reply schema:** `informal.trace/1`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `first` | integer | no | First frame (default 0) |
| `helpers` | boolean | no | Also give state the tool added to check the property |
| `last` | integer | no | Last frame (default: the last of the trace) |
| `name` | string | yes | Property name, exactly as property_list gives it |
| `signals` | array\<string\> | no | Globs on signal names (full path, path below the top, or last part) |

### `prove`

**Prove properties** — Run the engines on the named assertions and covers (the enabled ones of the task, or of the current task, when none is named) and return each one's result. Each task is proved on its own model, with its own assumptions and cut points. Only this gives a verdict. With wait=false it returns at once: follow with prove_status, end with prove_stop.

- **Availability:** All modes (`read-only`, `propose`, `auto`)
- **Mutates session:** no
- **Reply schema:** `informal.prove/1`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `properties` | array\<string\> | no | Names or globs |
| `task` | string | no | Prove this task's enabled assertions and covers (with properties: look the names up in it) |
| `time_limit_s` | number | no | Per property; the session's limit when left out, and never above the server's |
| `wait` | boolean | no | Default true |

### `prove_status`

**Progress of a prove** — Whether a prove is running, each property's state so far, and the result of the last prove started with wait=false once it has ended.

- **Availability:** All modes (`read-only`, `propose`, `auto`)
- **Mutates session:** no
- **Reply schema:** `informal.progress/1`

### `prove_stop`

**Stop a prove** — Ask a running prove to stop. Properties not settled yet become undetermined (stopped).

- **Availability:** All modes (`read-only`, `propose`, `auto`)
- **Mutates session:** no
- **Reply schema:** `informal.stop/1`

### `proposal_validate`

**Validate a candidate assumption, helper assertion, cover, or cut point** — Zero-side-effect scratch-task soundness oracle: tests a candidate `assume`, helper `assert` (lemma), `cover`, or `cut_point` BEFORE calling `proposal_add`. Checks syntax, SV-FPV-001 DUT-output over-constraint hygiene, bounded environment consistency + UNSAT conflict core, 2QBF dead-end trap states, vacuity, cover non-regression (`lost_covers`), and whether target assertions become `proven`. Leaves the live session completely untouched.

- **Availability:** All modes (`read-only`, `propose`, `auto`)
- **Mutates session:** no
- **Reply schema:** `informal.validate/1`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `check_covers` | boolean | no | Re-check existing covers to detect over-constraint (default: true for assume/cut_point) |
| `check_dead_end` | boolean | no | Run 2QBF dead-end trap-state detection on assumptions (default: true for assume) |
| `depth` | integer | no | Bounded environment check depth in model steps (default: 20) |
| `expr` | string | no | Property expression (for assume, assert, or cover) |
| `kind` | enum (`assume` \| `assert` \| `cover` \| `cut_point`) | yes |  |
| `name` | string | no | Optional property name |
| `signal` | string | no | Signal path to cut (for cut_point) |
| `targets` | array\<string\> | no | Optional target assertions to test impact on (default: all cex/undetermined assertions in current task) |
| `time_limit_s` | number | no | Per-property time limit in seconds (default: 15) |

### `proposal_add`

**Propose a change** — Propose an assumption, a helper assertion, a cover (`expr`, SystemVerilog in the top module's scope) or a cut point (`signal`). Call `proposal_validate` first to verify soundness, non-vacuity, and cover non-regression. In propose mode it waits for a person (state pending); in automatic mode it is applied at once, tagged AI-added.

- **Availability:** `propose` (waits for approval) / `auto` (applied immediately); hidden in `read-only`
- **Mutates session:** yes (by mode)
- **Reply schema:** `informal.proposal/1`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `expr` | string | no | Property expression, e.g. req \|=> gnt |
| `kind` | enum (`assume` \| `assert` \| `cover` \| `cut_point`) | yes |  |
| `name` | string | no | Name for the new property |
| `rationale` | string | yes | Why: shown to the person who decides |
| `signal` | string | no | Signal to cut from its drivers (cut_point) |

### `why_cex`

**Root-cause slice of a counterexample trace** — Dynamic backward slice from a falsified assertion (`cex`) or reached cover (`covered`) at failure frame T back to frame 0: walks only active mux arms (`ite`), controlling boolean operands, and register state transitions, pruning untaken datapaths and idle hold cycles.

- **Availability:** All modes (`read-only`, `propose`, `auto`)
- **Mutates session:** no
- **Reply schema:** `informal.why_cex/1`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `max_events` | integer | no | Maximum causal events to return (default 64) |
| `name` | string | yes | Property name |

### `cex_diagnose`

**Single-call counterexample root-cause dossier** — Preferred first tool for any `cex` or `covered` property: fuses `property_get`, backward `why_cex` causal slice, trimmed trace on active causal signals only, primary-input vs DUT-output/internal signal role classification, RTL driver source snippets (`signal_nav`), `formal_lint` findings, and a triage hint into one compact reply.

- **Availability:** All modes (`read-only`, `propose`, `auto`)
- **Mutates session:** no
- **Reply schema:** `informal.cex_diagnose/1`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `max_events` | integer | no | Maximum causal events (default: 24, max: 64) |
| `name` | string | yes | Property name (must have status cex or covered) |
| `source_context_lines` | integer | no | Context lines above/below each RTL driver (default: 4, max: 12) |
| `window` | integer | no | Cycles before failure_frame to include in active_trace (default: 6, max: 32) |

### `convergence_diagnose`

**Single-call proof convergence & complexity dossier** — Preferred first tool for `undetermined` or slow properties: fuses per-engine telemetry (`stats`, `max_bound`), COI input/register counts, `fv_complexity` arithmetic/memory/blackbox hotspots, active assumptions/cutpoints, and ranked proof-convergence tactics.

- **Availability:** All modes (`read-only`, `propose`, `auto`)

- **Reply schema:** `informal.convergence_diagnose/1`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | yes | Assert or cover property name |

### `spec_audit`

**Audit session against fvp.spec.json** — Cross-check the active session against a machine-verifiable formal verification spec (`fvp.spec.json` / `informal.spec/1`): verifies design/clock/reset intent, legal primary-input-only assumption boundary, per-requirement assertion + witness-cover status (`verified`, `cex`, `undetermined`, `missing_assert`, `missing_cover`, `vacuous`, `overconstrained`), signoff gates, and prioritized next actions. Auto-discovers `fvp.spec.json` next to the design files when `spec_file` and `spec` are omitted.

- **Availability:** All modes (`read-only`, `propose`, `auto`)
- **Mutates session:** no
- **Reply schema:** `informal.spec_audit/1`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `check_dead_end` | boolean | no | Run live environment consistency + 2QBF dead-end freedom check (default false) |
| `depth` | integer | no | Bounded depth for check_dead_end (default 10) |
| `mutation_score` | number | no | Optional mutant-kill percentage (0..100) to evaluate against signoff.mutation_score_floor |
| `spec` | object | no | Optional inline `informal.spec/1` JSON object instead of reading a file |
| `spec_file` | string | no | Optional path to fvp.spec.json (auto-discovered next to open design files when omitted) |
| `task` | string | no | Optional task name to audit (defaults to current_task) |

### `tcl_eval`

**Evaluate a Tcl command** — The escape hatch: evaluate a JasperGold or VC Formal style command in the session's shell. In automatic mode it runs; in propose mode it is recorded as a proposal that waits for a person (give `rationale`). Prefer the other tools: their replies are data.

- **Availability:** `propose` (waits for approval) / `auto` (applied immediately); hidden in `read-only`
- **Mutates session:** yes (by mode)
- **Reply schema:** `object`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `command` | string | yes |  |
| `rationale` | string | no | Why (required in propose mode) |

## Desktop Window Tools (`gui_*`)

Offered when connected to a running `InFormal.app` session (`informal mcp --connect`). Window tools drive visualization without mutating the formal model.

### `gui_state`

**What the person is looking at** — The window of the person working on this session: the property they selected, the view and layout preset, the open trace with their cursor's frame, callouts and signals, the source lines in view, schematic state, and any @-focus pills.

- **Availability:** Desktop window (`--connect` / InFormal.app), all modes
- **Mutates session:** no
- **Reply schema:** `informal.gui/1`

### `gui_select_property`

**Select a property in the window** — Select a property in the person's property table, as a click would: its details and source line show.

- **Availability:** Desktop window (`--connect` / InFormal.app), all modes
- **Mutates session:** no
- **Reply schema:** `informal.gui/1`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | yes | Property name |

### `gui_open_trace`

**Open a trace in the window** — Open the waveform of a property whose status is cex or covered in the person's window, with the cursor on `frame` (default: the frame where it fails or is hit). Use it to show the person the cycle you are talking about.

- **Availability:** Desktop window (`--connect` / InFormal.app), all modes
- **Mutates session:** no
- **Reply schema:** `informal.gui/1`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `frame` | integer | no | Frame for the cursor, from 0 |
| `name` | string | yes | Property name |

### `gui_add_signals`

**Add signals to the open waveform** — Add signals, by full name as trace_get gives them, to the waveform that is open in the person's window. Fails when no trace is open or a signal is not in that trace.

- **Availability:** Desktop window (`--connect` / InFormal.app), all modes
- **Mutates session:** no
- **Reply schema:** `informal.gui/1`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `signals` | array\<string\> | yes | Full signal names, e.g. fifo.u_wp.p |

### `gui_highlight_source`

**Show source lines in the window** — Open a design file or script in the person's source view and highlight a range of lines.

- **Availability:** Desktop window (`--connect` / InFormal.app), all modes
- **Mutates session:** no
- **Reply schema:** `informal.gui/1`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `file` | string | yes | Path, as a property's source or the summary's files give it |
| `first_line` | integer | yes | From 1 |
| `last_line` | integer | no | Default: first_line |

### `gui_set_view`

**Switch window view, layout preset, dock tab, or filter** — Switch the centre view (`table`, `source`, `trace`, `schematic`, `apps`), workspace layout preset (`triage`, `cex-debug`, `signoff`, `split`), Formal App tab (`cov`, `xprop`, `spv`, `sec`, `csr`, `protocol`), bottom dock tab, or property filter.

- **Availability:** Desktop window (`--connect` / InFormal.app), all modes
- **Mutates session:** no
- **Reply schema:** `informal.gui/1`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `app_tab` | enum (`cov` \| `xprop` \| `spv` \| `sec` \| `csr` \| `protocol`) | no | Formal Apps tab to select |
| `bottom_tab` | enum (`console` \| `details` \| `messages` \| `log` \| `info` \| `profiler` \| `apps` \| `proposals`) | no | Bottom dock tab |
| `filter` | string | no | Property filter text |
| `layout_preset` | enum (`triage` \| `cex-debug` \| `signoff` \| `split`) | no | Multi-pane workspace layout preset |
| `status_filter` | any | no | Status filter word or null to clear |
| `view` | enum (`table` \| `source` \| `trace` \| `schematic` \| `apps`) | no | Centre view to activate |

### `gui_toggle_why_cex`

**Toggle Why CEX causal root-cause slice overlay** — Open or close the `Why CEX` backward causal slice overlay on the open waveform, and optionally filter lanes to causal signals only (`slice_only`).

- **Availability:** Desktop window (`--connect` / InFormal.app), all modes
- **Mutates session:** no
- **Reply schema:** `informal.gui/1`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `open` | boolean | yes | Whether the Why CEX slice bar and cell highlights are shown |
| `slice_only` | boolean | no | Optional: show only signals in the active causal slice |

### `gui_annotate_trace`

**Pin AI callout badges onto waveform cells** — Pin visual callout badges onto specific `(signal, frame)` cells in the open waveform (or clear them) so the engineer sees exact root-cause transitions.

- **Availability:** Desktop window (`--connect` / InFormal.app), all modes
- **Mutates session:** no
- **Reply schema:** `informal.gui/1`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `annotations` | array\<object\> | no | Callout pins to show on the waveform |
| `clear` | boolean | no | Clear existing AI waveform callout pins |

### `gui_present_walkthrough`

**Present or step a guided multi-step CEX walkthrough** — Publish, step, or dismiss an interactive multi-step root-cause tour bar in the window that synchronizes the waveform cursor, callout pins, and RTL source lines on each step.

- **Availability:** Desktop window (`--connect` / InFormal.app), all modes
- **Mutates session:** no
- **Reply schema:** `informal.gui/1`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clear` | boolean | no | Dismiss the active walkthrough bar |
| `step` | integer | no | 0-based step index to jump to |
| `steps` | array\<object\> | no | Ordered walkthrough steps |
| `title` | string | no | Walkthrough title |

### `gui_open_schematic`

**Open the interactive COI & causal schematic** — Open the schematic viewer for property `name` (default: selected property) at `max_depth` register stages.

- **Availability:** Desktop window (`--connect` / InFormal.app), all modes
- **Mutates session:** no
- **Reply schema:** `informal.gui/1`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `max_depth` | integer | no | Optional register stage depth (default: 2) |
| `name` | string | no | Optional property name (defaults to selected property) |

### `gui_present_cex`

**Atomically present a synchronized CEX debug walkthrough** — Preferred single-call desktop visual tour for a `cex` or `covered` property: switches to `cex-debug` (or chosen layout preset), opens the trace at `frame`, activates the `Why CEX` causal slice, pins AI callout badges, and launches the interactive walkthrough bar. Auto-synthesizes steps and callouts from `why_cex` when omitted.

- **Availability:** Desktop window (`--connect` / InFormal.app), all modes
- **Mutates session:** no
- **Reply schema:** `informal.gui/1`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `annotations` | array\<object\> | no | Optional custom waveform callout badges (auto-generated from why_cex if omitted) |
| `capture` | boolean | no | Also capture a standalone trace SVG into window.capture (default: false) |
| `frame` | integer | no | Optional initial cursor frame (default: failure_frame) |
| `layout_preset` | enum (`triage` \| `cex-debug` \| `signoff` \| `split`) | no | Workspace layout preset (default: cex-debug) |
| `name` | string | yes | Property name (status cex or covered) |
| `slice_only` | boolean | no | Filter waveform lanes to active causal signals only (default: false) |
| `steps` | array\<object\> | no | Optional custom walkthrough steps (auto-generated from why_cex if omitted) |
| `title` | string | no | Optional walkthrough title (default: Why <name> fails) |

### `gui_capture_view`

**Capture deterministic SVG or visual summary of the active view** — Render a standalone SVG of the open waveform or schematic (including Why CEX highlights and AI callout badges) into `window.capture` for visual verification or Markdown reports.

- **Availability:** Desktop window (`--connect` / InFormal.app), all modes
- **Mutates session:** no
- **Reply schema:** `informal.gui/1`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `target` | enum (`trace` \| `schematic` \| `window`) | no | View to capture (default: trace) |
